title: Trade Board Inventory Separation
lede: Students can now tell whether they are taking over another student's posted shift or requesting an unassigned open slot before they act.

stats.n: The same two fixture records now retain their source meaning
Trade claim and open-slot pickup still wait for Admin approval

sections.heading: Student-posted trades
sections.note: Same iPhone 16 Pro, role, fixture data, and automated scroll target.

pairs.title: A named student's coverage request
pairs.sub: The row identifies Priya as the poster and retains the trade-specific claim action.
pairs.beforeCap: Was: the trade sat in one mixed Available Now pool beside an unassigned slot.
pairs.afterCap: Now: Trade Posts establishes that this is a person-to-person coverage request.

sections.heading: Unassigned open shifts
sections.note: The open Student slot is the same fixture record in both captures.

pairs.title: A published slot with nobody assigned
pairs.sub: The row keeps its open-slot claim action and separate pickup-request consequence.
pairs.beforeCap: Was: the open slot and trade post shared the same Available Now heading.
pairs.afterCap: Now: Open Shifts names the inventory and explains that claiming sends a pickup request.

changes.was: Available Now merged unassigned Student slots and student-posted trades, even though they come from different records and have different human meaning.
changes.now: Trade Posts and Open Shifts have independent headings, counts, and consequence copy on native iOS and web.

changes.h: The summary counted shifts, not decisions
changes.was: The native summary called both record types shifts available, reinforcing the idea that they were one inventory.
changes.now: The summary counts opportunities and points students to the two source-specific sections below.

verification: Matched iOS UI test: source-control baseline and changed source both passed on iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 26.5, using the same deterministic fixture.
35 focused tests pass across Trade Board, Open Work, Admin review, student field, and consequence-copy contracts.
TypeScript, full ESLint, and the 253-page app build pass; iOS project integrity, drift, audit-gap, and pinned iPhone 16 Pro build checks pass.
Docs: codemaps are current and repository documentation verification passes.
notes: The Admin review queue and the student's Waiting on Admin section intentionally remain unified because both claim types have the same review and recovery job.
No production data was read or mutated. Authenticated web rendering, deployment, TestFlight, and physical-device acceptance remain separate gates.
